sentences.zh: 成千載之大義，遂我初心。

translations.literal: complete the great righteousness of a thousand ages and fulfill my original intent.
translations.idiomatic: complete the great righteousness of a thousand ages and fulfill my original intent.

sentences.zh: 爾其永保兆民，勉持一德，慎乃有位，允執厥中。

translations.literal: You shall forever preserve the myriad people, strive to hold to one virtue, be careful in your position, and truly hold fast to the center.
translations.idiomatic: Forever preserve the myriad people, strive to hold to one virtue, be careful in your position, and truly hold fast to the center.

sentences.zh: 亦惟無疆之休，其誡之哉！

translations.literal: May there also be boundless blessing—take this as your warning!
translations.idiomatic: May there also be boundless blessing. Take this as your warning!

sentences.zh: 禮畢，帝鼓吹道從而歸。

translations.literal: When the ceremony was complete, the Emperor returned with drums and pipes clearing the road before him.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony was complete, the Emperor returned with drums and pipes clearing the road before him.

sentences.zh: 始梁開國之歲，即前唐天祐四年也，潞州行營使李思安奏：「壺關縣庶穰鄉鄉人伐樹，樹倒自分兩片，內有六字如左書，云『天十四載石進』。」

translations.literal: In the year when Liang first founded its state, which was the fourth year of Tianyou of former Tang, Lu prefecture campaign commissioner Li Si'an memorialized: "In Shurang township of Huguan county, when villagers felled a tree, the tree split of itself into two pieces, and within were six characters like writing in seal script, reading 'Heaven, fourteenth year, Shi advances.'
translations.idiomatic: In the year when Liang first founded its state, the fourth year of Tianyou of former Tang, Lu prefecture campaign commissioner Li Si'an memorialized: "In Shurang township of Huguan county, when villagers felled a tree, it split of itself into two pieces. Within were six characters in seal script reading 'Heaven, fourteenth year, Shi advances.'

sentences.zh: 梁祖令藏於武庫，然莫詳其義。

translations.literal: The Liang founder ordered it stored in the armory, yet none could make clear its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang founder ordered it stored in the armory, yet none could make clear its meaning.

sentences.zh: 至帝即位，識者曰：「『天』字取『四』字中兩畫加之於傍，則『丙』字也；

translations.literal: When the Emperor took the throne, those who understood said: "If one takes the two strokes from the middle of the character for 'four' in the character for 'Heaven' and adds them to the side, one gets the character for 'bing';
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor took the throne, those who understood said: "If one takes the two strokes from the middle of the character for 'four' in the character for 'Heaven' and adds them to the side, one gets the character for 'bing';

sentences.zh: 『四』字去中之兩畫，加『十』字，則『申』字也。」

translations.literal: if one removes the two middle strokes from the character for 'four' and adds the character for 'ten,' one gets the character for 'shen.'
translations.idiomatic: if one removes the two middle strokes from the character for 'four' and adds the character for 'ten,' one gets the character for 'shen.'

sentences.zh: 帝即位之年乃丙申也。

translations.literal: The year the Emperor took the throne was indeed bingshen.
translations.idiomatic: The year the Emperor took the throne was indeed bingshen.

sentences.zh: 又，《易》云：「晉者，進也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the Book of Changes says: "Jin means advance."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Book of Changes says: "Jin means advance."

sentences.zh: 國號大晉，皆符契焉。

translations.literal: The state name Great Jin all accorded with these tokens.
translations.idiomatic: The state name Great Jin accorded with all of these tokens.

sentences.zh: 又，帝即位之前一年，歲在乙未，鄴西有柵曰李固，清、淇合流在其側。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the year before the Emperor took the throne, the year was yiwei; west of Ye there was a stockade called Liguo, where the Qing and Qi rivers joined beside it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the year before the Emperor took the throne, the year was yiwei. West of Ye there was a stockade called Liguo, where the Qing and Qi rivers joined beside it.

sentences.zh: 柵有橋，橋下大鼠與蛇鬥，鬥及日之申，蛇不勝而死。

translations.literal: The stockade had a bridge; below the bridge a great rat and a snake fought, and the fight lasted until the hour of shen, when the snake could not prevail and died.
translations.idiomatic: The stockade had a bridge. Below the bridge a great rat and a snake fought until the hour of shen, when the snake could not prevail and died.

sentences.zh: 行人觀者數百，識者誌之。

translations.literal: Several hundred passersby watched, and those who understood recorded it.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred passersby watched, and those who understood recorded it.

sentences.zh: 後唐末帝果滅於申。

translations.literal: Later Tang's Last Emperor was indeed destroyed in the hour of shen.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tang's Last Emperor was indeed destroyed at the hour of shen.

sentences.zh: 又，末帝，真定常山人也，有先人舊廬，其側有古佛剎，剎有石像，忽搖動不已，人皆異之。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Last Emperor was a man of Zhending and Changshan; he had an ancestral old residence, and beside it an ancient Buddhist monastery with a stone image that suddenly shook without cease, and all regarded it as strange.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Last Emperor was from Zhending in Changshan. He had an ancestral residence, and beside it stood an ancient Buddhist monastery with a stone image that suddenly shook without cease. All regarded it as strange.

sentences.zh: 及重圍晉陽，帝遣心腹何福輕騎求援北蕃，蕃主自將諸部赴之。

translations.literal: When Jinyang was heavily besieged, the Emperor sent his trusted man He Fu with light cavalry to seek aid from the northern barbarians; the barbarian ruler personally led the various tribes to come.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinyang was heavily besieged, the Emperor sent his trusted man He Fu with light cavalry to seek aid from the northern tribes. The Khitan ruler personally led his tribes to come.

sentences.zh: 不以繒帛，不以珠金，若響應聲。

translations.literal: Without silks, without pearls and gold, he came like an echo answering a sound.
translations.idiomatic: Without silks, without pearls and gold, he came like an echo answering a sound.

sentences.zh: 謂福曰：「吾已兆於夢，皆上帝命我，非我意也。」

translations.literal: He said to Fu: "I have already been foretold in a dream; all is the Supreme Lord's command to me, not my own intent."
translations.idiomatic: He said to Fu: "I have already been foretold in a dream. All of this is the Supreme Lord's command to me, not my own intent."

sentences.zh: （《契丹國志》引《紀異錄》云：契丹主德光常晝寢，夢一神人花冠美姿容，輜梅甚盛，忽自天而下，衣白衣，佩金帶，執钅骨钅朵，有異人十二隨其後，內一黑兔入德光懷而失之。

translations.literal: (The Khitan State Annals cites the Record of Strange Events: The Khitan ruler Deguang often napped by day and dreamed of a divine man with a flowered crown and beautiful countenance, with very abundant plum blossoms in his carriage, who suddenly descended from Heaven, wore white robes, bore a golden belt, and grasped an axe; twelve strange men followed behind him, and among them a black rabbit entered Deguang's bosom and was lost.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Khitan State Annals》 cites the 《Record of Strange Events》: The Khitan ruler Deguang often napped by day and dreamed of a divine man with a flowered crown and beautiful countenance, with very abundant plum blossoms in his carriage, who suddenly descended from Heaven, wore white robes, bore a golden belt, and grasped an axe. Twelve strange men followed behind him, and among them a black rabbit entered Deguang's bosom and vanished.

sentences.zh: 神人語德光曰：「石郎使人喚汝，汝須去。」

translations.literal: The divine man said to Deguang: "Master Shi has sent men to summon you; you must go."
translations.idiomatic: The divine man said to Deguang: "Master Shi has sent men to summon you. You must go."

sentences.zh: 覺告其母，母忽之，不以為異。

translations.literal: When he awoke he told his mother; his mother dismissed it and did not regard it as strange.
translations.idiomatic: When he awoke he told his mother. She dismissed it and did not regard it as strange.

sentences.zh: 後復夢，即前神人也，衣冠儀貌，儼然如故，曰：「石郎已使人來喚汝。」

translations.literal: Later he dreamed again—it was the same divine man as before, robes, cap, bearing, and appearance all exactly as before, who said: "Master Shi has already sent men to summon you."
translations.idiomatic: Later he dreamed again. It was the same divine man as before, robes, cap, bearing, and appearance all exactly as before, who said: "Master Shi has already sent men to summon you."

sentences.zh: 既覺而驚，復以告母。

translations.literal: When he awoke he was alarmed and again told his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When he awoke he was alarmed and again told his mother.

sentences.zh: 母曰：「可命筮。」

translations.literal: His mother said: "You may order divination."
translations.idiomatic: His mother said: "You may order divination."

sentences.zh: 乃召巫筮，言：「太祖從西樓來，言中國將立天王，要爾為助，爾須去。」

translations.literal: He thereupon summoned a shaman to divine, who said: "The Founding Ancestor comes from the Western Tower and says China will establish a Heavenly King and wants you to assist; you must go."
translations.idiomatic: He summoned a shaman to divine, who said: "The Founding Ancestor comes from the Western Tower and says China will establish a Heavenly King and wants you to assist. You must go."

sentences.zh: 未浹旬，唐石敬瑭反於河東，為後唐張敬達所敗，亟遣趙瑩持表重賂，許割燕雲，求兵為援，契丹主曰：「我非為石郎興師，乃奉天帝敕使也。」）〉

translations.literal: Before ten days had passed, Tang's Shi Jingtang rebelled in Hedong, was defeated by Later Tang's Zhang Jingda, and urgently sent Zhao Ying with a memorial and heavy bribes, promising to cede Yan and Yun and seeking troops as aid; the Khitan ruler said, "I do not raise troops for Master Shi; I obey the Heavenly Emperor's command.".)〉
translations.idiomatic: Before ten days had passed, Tang's Shi Jingtang rebelled in Hedong, was defeated by Later Tang's Zhang Jingda, and urgently sent Zhao Ying with a memorial and heavy bribes, promising to cede Yan and Yun and seeking troops as aid. The Khitan ruler said, "I do not raise troops for Master Shi. I obey the Heavenly Emperor's command.".)〉

sentences.zh: 時援兵未至，偽將張敬達引軍逼城設柵，柵將成，必有大風暴雨，柵無以立。

translations.literal: At that time relief troops had not yet arrived; the rebel general Zhang Jingda led troops pressing the city and set up stockades; whenever the stockades were about to be completed, great wind and violent rain would come, and the stockades could not stand.
translations.idiomatic: At that time relief troops had not yet arrived. The rebel general Zhang Jingda led troops against the city and set up stockades. Whenever the stockades were about to be completed, great wind and violent rain would come, and the stockades could not stand.

sentences.zh: 後築長城，城就，又為水潦所壞，城終不能合。

translations.literal: Later they built a long wall; when the wall was completed it was again destroyed by flooding, and the wall in the end could not be joined.
translations.idiomatic: Later they built a long wall. When the wall was completed it was again destroyed by flooding, and the wall in the end could not be joined.

sentences.zh: 晉陽有北宮，宮城之上有祠曰毗沙門天王，帝曾焚修默而禱之。

translations.literal: Jinyang had a Northern Palace; above the palace city was a shrine to Vaisravana, the Heavenly King; the Emperor once burned incense, performed repairs, and prayed to it in silence.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyang had a Northern Palace. Above the palace city was a shrine to Vaisravana, the Heavenly King. The Emperor once burned incense, performed repairs, and prayed to it in silence.

sentences.zh: 經數日，城西北正受敵處，軍候報稱，夜來有一人長丈餘，介金執殳，行於城上，久方不見。

translations.literal: After several days, at the northwest of the city where the enemy pressed directly, military scouts reported that in the night a man more than ten feet tall, armored in gold and grasping a halberd, walked upon the city wall and only after a long while was no longer seen.
translations.idiomatic: After several days, at the northwest of the city where the enemy pressed directly, military scouts reported that in the night a man more than ten feet tall, armored in gold and grasping a halberd, walked upon the city wall and only after a long while vanished from sight.

sentences.zh: 帝心異之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was astonished in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was astonished.

sentences.zh: 又，牙城有僧坊曰崇福，坊之廡下西北隅有泥神，神之首忽一日有煙生，其騰郁如曲突之狀。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the garrison city was a monks' quarter called Chongfu; in the northwest corner beneath its cloister walk was a clay spirit, and one day smoke suddenly arose from the spirit's head, rising thick like smoke from a bent chimney.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the garrison city was a monks' quarter called Chongfu. In the northwest corner beneath its cloister walk stood a clay spirit, and one day smoke suddenly arose from the spirit's head, rising thick like smoke from a bent chimney.

sentences.zh: 坊僧奔赴，以為人火所延，及俯而視之，無所有焉。

translations.literal: The monks of the quarter rushed there, thinking human fire had spread, but when they bent down to look, there was nothing at all.
translations.idiomatic: The monks of the quarter rushed there, thinking human fire had spread, but when they bent down to look, there was nothing at all.

sentences.zh: 事尋達帝，帝召僧之臘高者問焉，僧曰：「貧道見莊宗將得天下，曾有此煙。

translations.literal: The matter soon reached the Emperor; he summoned the monk of highest monastic standing and asked him, and the monk said: "This humble priest saw when Zhuangzong was about to gain the realm that there was once this smoke.
translations.idiomatic: The matter soon reached the Emperor. He summoned the monk of highest monastic standing and asked him. The monk said: "This humble priest saw when Zhuangzong was about to gain the realm that there was once this smoke.

sentences.zh: 觀此噴湧，甚於當時，兆可知矣。」

translations.literal: Observing this gushing forth, it is greater than at that time—the omen can be known."
translations.idiomatic: Observing this gushing forth, it is greater than at that time. The omen can be known."

sentences.zh: 自此，日旁多有五色雲氣，如蓮芰之狀。

translations.literal: From this time, beside the sun there were often five-colored clouds in the shape of lotus leaves.
translations.idiomatic: From this time, beside the sun there were often five-colored clouds in the shape of lotus leaves.

sentences.zh: 帝召占者視之，謂曰：「此驗應誰？」

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned diviners to observe them and said: "For whom is this sign fulfilled?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned diviners to observe them and said: "For whom is this sign fulfilled?"

sentences.zh: 占者曰：「見處為瑞，更應何人！」

translations.literal: The diviners said: "Where it is seen is where the auspice falls—for whom else could it be!"
translations.idiomatic: The diviners said: "Where it is seen is where the auspice falls. For whom else could it be!"

sentences.zh: 又，帝每詰旦使慰撫守陴者，率以為常。

translations.literal: Moreover, every dawn the Emperor sent men to comfort and reassure those guarding the battlements, and this was his constant practice.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, every dawn the Emperor sent men to comfort and reassure those guarding the battlements, and this was his constant practice.

sentences.zh: 忽一夕已暝，城上有號令之聲，聲不絕者三。

translations.literal: Suddenly one night, already dark, there were sounds of commands on the wall, and the sounds did not cease for three rounds.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly one night, already dark, there were sounds of commands on the wall, and the sounds did not cease for three rounds.

sentences.zh: 帝使人問之，將吏云：「從上傳來者。」

translations.literal: The Emperor sent men to ask about it; the generals and officers said: "They come transmitted from above."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent men to ask about it. The generals and officers said: "They come transmitted from above."

sentences.zh: 皆知神助。

translations.literal: All knew it was divine assistance.
translations.idiomatic: All knew it was divine assistance.

sentences.zh: 時城中復有數家井泉，暴溢不止。

translations.literal: At that time within the city several households' wells and springs also overflowed violently without cease.
translations.idiomatic: At that time within the city several households' wells and springs also overflowed violently without cease.

sentences.zh: 及蕃軍大至，合勢破之，末帝之眾，似拉朽焉。

translations.literal: When the barbarian army arrived in great force and joined strength to break them, the Last Emperor's host was like pulling rotten wood apart.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan army arrived in great force and joined strength to break them, the Last Emperor's host collapsed like rotten wood pulled apart.

sentences.zh: 斯天運使然，非人力也。

translations.literal: This was Heaven's turning made so—it was not human power.
translations.idiomatic: This was Heaven's turning made so. It was not human power.

sentences.zh: 是日，帝言於契丹主，願以雁門已北及幽州之地為戎王壽，仍約歲輸帛三十萬，戎王許之。

translations.literal: That day the Emperor spoke to the Khitan ruler, wishing to give the lands north of Yanmen and Youzhou as a gift for the Rong king's longevity, and also agreed to deliver three hundred thousand bolts of silk yearly; the Rong king consented.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Emperor spoke to the Khitan ruler, offering the lands north of Yanmen and Youzhou as a gift for the Khitan ruler's longevity and agreeing to deliver three hundred thousand bolts of silk yearly. The Khitan ruler consented.
